questions.heading: A Budget and Yes-or-No Choices Make a 0-1 Knapsack
questions.stem: A teammate wants to replace the MathOpt model with a ranking by risk per $k, since on the small season the two plans differ by only $8k a year. What reason does the lesson give for keeping the model?

options.text: The ranking spends more than the budget on the small season
options.says: The ranking stops with $26k unspent: it keeps the budget.

options.text: Later requirements add rules, and a model takes each as a new row
options.says: Right: the MILP was chosen because every later requirement is one more row or variable, not a new algorithm.

options.text: The ranking picks fewer circuits than the model on the small season
options.says: Both pick nine circuits; they differ by one swap.

options.text: The ranking needs a solver to sort the twenty circuits by ratio
options.says: A ranking is a spreadsheet answer anyone can check; it needs no solver.

questions.heading: The Change, File by File
questions.stem: HiGHS ends a solve of make_plan with the termination reason INFEASIBLE. What does the lesson's make_plan return?

options.text: It raises an exception that the caller must catch and report
options.says: make_plan never raises for a status: no plan is an answer the caller handles.

options.text: A plan with each listed circuit trimmed and status FEASIBLE
options.says: Only OPTIMAL and FEASIBLE results are read into trims; other statuses give an empty plan.

options.text: The last plan HiGHS found, with the status set to INFEASIBLE
options.says: No trims are read from a result that is not OPTIMAL or FEASIBLE.

options.text: An empty plan that carries the status INFEASIBLE to the caller
options.says: Right: a status other than OPTIMAL or FEASIBLE returns Plan(status), with no trims.

questions.heading: Four Tests Pin the Requirement Down
questions.stem: Of the four tests the lesson adds, it calls the brute-force test on the tiny season the strongest. Why?

options.text: It checks the optimum against an answer found without a solver
options.says: Right: it compares with the best of all 64 subsets, computed in plain Python.

options.text: It is the one test that runs on a season from the generator
options.says: The budget test also runs on a generated season, the small one.

options.text: It is the one test that fails against the skeleton steps/00
options.says: The output shows all four new tests failing against steps/00.

options.text: It covers the zero-budget case that the other tests leave out
options.says: A separate test covers the zero budget.
